# Kanban syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-kanban/grammar/kanban.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Kanban syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `kanban` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text that no rule takes apart; and a line break appended. Keywords are matched without
regard to case.

The first item's indent is the column level: an item at that indent is a column, and any other
item is a card of the last column, at any depth; an item indented less than the first is an
error once another item follows it. `@{ … }` after an item is its YAML data. A `:::class` or
`::icon(…)` line decorates the last item written before it. A blank or comment line counts as a
statement where one may start, so an item right after two of them in a row, or one right after
`kanban`, is an error, as in mermaid@12.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A kanban board is `kanban`, then its statements, each followed by a line break, a blank
line or the end. Blank and comment lines may come before `kanban`.

```ebnf
diagram = [ SPACELINE { SPACELINE | NL } ] KANBAN [ NL ] statement stop { statement stop } ;
```

```ebnf
stop = ( NL | EOF | SPACELINE ) { NL | EOF } ;
```

```ebnf
statement = SPACELIST [ Item | Icon | Class ]
          | SPACELINE
          | Item
          | Icon
          | Class ;
```

An item, a column or a card by its indent: an id, a shape with its text, or both (`todo`,
`id[text]`, `[text]`), then optional shape data (`id@{ ticket: T-1 }`).

```ebnf
Item @Item = node [ shapeData ] ;
```

```ebnf
node = NODE_ID [ shape ]
     | shape ;
```

```ebnf
shape = NODE_DSTART NODE_DESCR NODE_DEND ;
```

Back-to-back blocks (`@{…}@{…}`) are joined into one before the YAML is read.

```ebnf
shapeData = SHAPE_DATA { SHAPE_DATA } ;
```

`::icon(…)`: the icon of the last item, on a line of its own.

```ebnf
Icon = ICON ;
```

`:::class …`: the classes of the last item, on a line of its own; a later one replaces them.

```ebnf
Class = CLASS ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `class`, `icon`, `node`, `nstr`, `nstr2`, `shapeData`, `shapeDataStr`.

Every rule ignores case: a rule for `ab` also matches `AB` and `aB`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | SHAPE_DATA | `@\{` | push(shapeData) empty | Shape data `@{ … }`: the item's YAML data (`ticket`, `assigned`, `priority`, `label`, `icon`, `shape`); line breaks in a quoted value read as `<br/>`. |
| shapeData | SHAPE_DATA | `"` | push(shapeDataStr) |  |
| shapeDataStr | SHAPE_DATA | `"` | pop |  |
| shapeDataStr | SHAPE_DATA | `[^"]+` | fold |  |
| shapeData | SHAPE_DATA | `[^}^"]+` |  |  |
| shapeData | — | `\}` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | SPACELINE | `\s*%%.*` |  | A `%%` comment v12's comment removal left (after text on a line, or a bare `%%`), with the blanks and line breaks before it: a blank line. |
| INITIAL | KANBAN | `kanban\b` |  | `kanban`: starts a kanban board; its columns and cards follow, one per line. |
| INITIAL | — | `:::` | push(class) | `:::class …`: the classes of the last item, the rest of the line. |
| class | CLASS | `.+` | pop |  |
| class | — | `\n` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | — | `::icon\(` | push(icon) | `::icon(…)`: the icon of the last item, up to `)`. Kept, but not drawn. |
| INITIAL | SPACELINE | `[\s]+[\n]` |  | Blanks up to the last line break of their run: a blank line. |
| INITIAL | NL | `[\n]+` |  |  |
| icon | ICON | `[^\)]+` |  |  |
| icon | — | `\)` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `-\)` | push(node) | A shape opener: `[`, `(`, `((`, `)`, `))`, `{{`, `-)` or `(-`. Every shape draws the same card or column. |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\(-` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\)\)` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\)` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\(\(` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\{\{` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\(` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | NODE_DSTART | `\[` | push(node) |  |
| INITIAL | SPACELIST | `[\s]+` |  | The indent before an item: the first item's sets the column level. |
| INITIAL | NODE_ID | `[^\(\[\n\)\{\}@]+` |  | An item id, which may hold blanks: the text up to a shape opener, `@` or the line end. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |
| node | — | `["][`]` | push(nstr2) | Strings in a shape: `"…"` and markdown strings `` "`…`" ``. |
| nstr2 | NODE_DESCR | `[^`"]+` |  |  |
| nstr2 | — | `[`]["]` | pop |  |
| node | — | `["]` | push(nstr) |  |
| nstr | NODE_DESCR | `[^"]+` |  |  |
| nstr | — | `["]` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `[\)]\)` | pop | A shape closer: any of them closes any shape. |
| node | NODE_DEND | `[\)]` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `[\]]` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `\}\}` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `\(-` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `-\)` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `\(\(` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DEND | `\(` | pop |  |
| node | NODE_DESCR | `[^\)\]\(\}]+` |  | An item's text: up to a closer, over line breaks; a `}` takes the rest of its line. |
| node | NODE_DESCR | `.+(?!\(\()` |  |  |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
